reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports DDR-driven grain refinement in a Co-containing TRIP-HEA under hot compression, but it does not address the Co-free FeNiCrMn system, nor does it establish that DDR enhances ductility or that a DDR-to-slip/twinning transition governs dynamic behavior in this alloy. The key premises that extend the mechanism to FeNiCrMn and link DDR to ductility are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: DDR is an important grain-refinement mechanism in HEAs at higher temperature and lower strain rate
DDR activation depends on temperature and strain rate via the Zener–Hollomon parameter
DDR enhances ductility while dislocation slip and twinning preserve strength
The Co-free FeNiCrMn system can exhibit the same DDR-dominated mechanism as Co-containing HEAs
The dynamic response of FeNiCrMn is governed by a transition between DDR and slip/twinning
